hindi: हे इन्द्र, वृत्रहन्, अब हमारे पास, हमारे भाग की ओर आओ, तुम महान्, महान् सहायताओं के साथ।
english: Come now to us, O Indra, Vṛtra-slayer, to our portion, you the great, with great helps.
notes: ardha is taken as 'portion/share' (could also be 'side'). The preverb ā appears twice, translated once as 'come'.

hindi: तुम निश्चय ही फुर्तीले और प्रेरित करने वाले हो; हे अद्भुत, अद्भुत स्त्रियों में तुम सहायता के लिए अद्भुत को बनाते हो।
english: You are indeed quick, impelling; O wonderful one, among the wonderful ones you make the wonderful for help.
notes: UNCLEAR. bhṛmi (quick/whirling) and tūtuji (impelling) are glossed from dictionary senses; citriṇīṣu is a feminine locative plural whose referent is not stated; the two ā are left as preverbs and not translated into a firm construction. The sense is given only literally.

words.gram: m. acc. sg. pres. part. form and sense uncertain

hindi: छोटे साथियों के साथ तुम बल से बढ़ते हुए, और भी बड़े को मार गिराते हो, उन मित्रों के साथ जो तुम्हारे साथ हैं।
english: With small ones you smite even the greater one, growing great with strength, with friends who are together with you.
notes: UNCLEAR: śaśīyāṃsam (taken as 'greater'; could be 'more numerous'), vrādhantam (taken as 'growing great'), and dabhrebhiḥ (masc. 'small ones', referent unstated). 'tve sacā' read as 'together with you'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हम तुम्हारे साथ हैं; हम तुम्हारी ओर पुकार रहे हैं; हमें, हमें ही ऊपर उठाकर सहायता करो।
english: We, O Indra, are together with you; we cry out to you; help us up, us indeed.
notes: 'vayam ... tve sacā' has no verb; 'are' is supplied by the construction. nonumaḥ is an intensive of √nu 'cry out, praise'. ut ... ava is taken as 'help up' (ud-√av); this is the only literal reading, not certain.

hindi: वही तुम हमारे पास अद्भुत, निर्दोष, अपराजित सहायताओं के साथ आओ, हे पत्थर के स्वामी।
english: Such as you are, come to us with wonderful, blameless, unassailed helps, O possessor of the stone.
notes: adri = stone (also 'mountain'); adrivaḥ is the literal 'possessing a stone'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हम तुम जैसे के मित्र बनें, गायों से भरे, पुरस्कार के लिए जुड़े हुए साथी, उस उत्साही पुरस्कार के लिए।
english: May we indeed be friends of one like you, O Indra, rich in cows, partners for the lively prize.
notes: ghṛṣvaye is taken with vājāya ('lively prize'); it could be a separate dative 'for the lively one'.

hindi: क्योंकि हे इन्द्र, तुम अकेले गायों से भरे पुरस्कार के स्वामी हो; वही तुम हमें महान् स्फूर्ति दो।
english: For you alone, O Indra, are master of the prize rich in cows; such as you are, grant us great refreshment.

text_flags.why: possible: the usual 2 sg. middle ending is -e; printed ending -a

hindi: जब तुम स्तुति किए जाकर स्तोताओं को दान देना चाहते हो, तब वे तुम्हें किसी और प्रकार से नहीं रोकते, हे इन्द्र, स्तुति के प्रेमी।
english: They do not hold you back otherwise when you, praised, wish to give bounty to the singers, O Indra, delighting in hymns.
notes: The subject of varante is not stated; 'they' is the unavoidable 3 pl. subject. anyathā 'otherwise' could mean 'in any other way'. magha = bounty.

hindi: गोतमों ने तुम्हारी ओर स्तुति से पुकारा है, देने के लिए, हे इन्द्र, उस उत्साही पुरस्कार के लिए।
english: The Gotamas have cried out forth to you with a hymn, for giving, O Indra, for the lively prize.
notes: 'abhi ... pra anūṣata' both preverbs of √nu; dāvane taken as dative 'for giving' (dāvan). The Gotamas are a family/group of sages. gotamāḥ is a name.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. mid. √mand

hindi: हम तुम्हारे वीर कार्य बताएँ, जिन्हें मत्त होकर तुमने तोड़ा, दास के गढ़ों को, उन पर चढ़ाई करके।
english: Let us proclaim your heroic deeds, which you, exhilarated, broke open — the Dāsa strongholds, having gone against them.
notes: yā is taken as referring to the strongholds (f. acc. pl.) in apposition; it could also stand for yāni (heroic deeds). dāsīḥ is the feminine adjective 'of the Dāsa(s)'. abhītya may be 'having overcome'.

hindi: तुम्हारे वे कार्य, जो तुमने किए, वे वीर पौरुष के कार्य, भक्त जन गाते हैं, निचोड़े हुए रसों में, हे इन्द्र, स्तुति के प्रेमी।
english: Those manly deeds of yours which you have done, the devout hymn, among the pressed ones, O Indra, delighting in hymns.
notes: vedhasaḥ rendered 'the devout'. suteṣu 'in/among the pressed (offerings)', the noun is not stated; rendered as 'the pressed ones'. 'those ... which you have done' are the object of gṛṇanti.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, स्तोम ढोने वाले गोतम तुममें बलवान् हुए हैं; इन पर वीरों से युक्त यश स्थापित करो।
english: The Gotamas, bearers of praise, have grown strong in you, O Indra; set upon these glory rich in heroes.
notes: avīvṛdhanta may also be transitive ('have strengthened you'); read as intransitive middle. aiṣu = ā + eṣu.

hindi: क्योंकि हे इन्द्र, तुम बहुतों के लिए समान हो; ऐसे तुम्हें हम पुकारते हैं।
english: Since, O Indra, you are indeed common to the many, as such we call on you.
notes: śaśvat is taken as 'many' (it can also mean 'every, perpetual'); the phrase is therefore uncertain. sādhāraṇa 'common, shared by all'.

hindi: हमारी ओर मुड़े हुए, हे उत्तम, हमारे लिए रहो; पेय से भली-भाँति मत्त हो, सोमों के, हे इन्द्र, सोम पीने वाले।
english: Turned towards us, O good one, be for us; be well exhilarated by the draught of the Somas, O Indra, Soma-drinker.
notes: vaso is read as the vocative of vasu ('good one'; could also be 'O lord of wealth'). somānām 'of the Somas' is literal; andhasaḥ is genitive after mad.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हमारे विचारों की स्तुति तुम्हें यहाँ लाए; दोनों भूरे-पीले घोड़ों को इस ओर घुमाओ।
english: O Indra, may the praise of our thoughts bring you here; turn the two tawny horses this way.
notes: asmākam can go with stoma or matīnām. ā yacchatu is read as ā-√yam 'bring'.

words.gram: 2 sg. caus. mid. subj. √juṣ form uncertain

hindi: हमारा पुरोडाश खाओ और हमारी स्तुतियों में आनन्द लो, जैसे वधू की चाह रखने वाला युवती में।
english: And eat our puroḍāśa cake, and take pleasure in our hymns, like one desiring a bride, a young woman.
notes: puroḍāśa is the name of an oblation cake, kept as a term. joṣayāse (form uncertain, taken as 2 sg. of juṣ 'enjoy'). The simile 'vadhūyuḥ iva yoṣaṇām' is taken as 'like one desiring a bride takes pleasure in a young woman'. The text of the verb 'ghasaḥ' is injunctive and read as imperative sense.

words.gram: f. gen. pl. form and sense uncertain

hindi: हम इन्द्र से माँगते हैं एक हज़ार, चलने वालों और जुते हुओं में से, और सोम की सौ खारियाँ।
english: We beseech Indra for a thousand of the passing ones, of the yoked, a hundred measures of Soma.
notes: UNCLEAR: vyatīnām (form and referent unknown); khārī is a measure of capacity (rendered 'measure'). The object of the thousand is not stated. īmahe 'we beseech' (√ī 'ask, seek'?) is uncertain.

hindi: तुम्हारे हज़ारों और सैकड़ों गायों को हम यहाँ चलाते हैं; तुम्हारी उदारता हमारे बीच आए।
english: Your thousands and hundreds of cows we set moving hither; may your bounty come among us.
notes: te in the first half may go with rādhaḥ instead. cyāvayāmasi 'we set in motion, drive'.

words.gram: 1 pl. opt. mid. form and root uncertain

hindi: तुम्हारे दस कलशों के सोने को हम पाएँ; तुम बहुत देने वाले हो, हे वृत्रहन्।
english: May we obtain ten of your jars of gold; you are a giver of much, O Vṛtra-slayer.
notes: UNCLEAR: adhīmahi (root unclear; taken as 'we would obtain'); the double genitive 'kalaśānām hiraṇyānām' is rendered 'jars of gold'.

hindi: हे बहुत देने वाले, हमें बहुत दो; थोड़ा नहीं, बहुत लाओ; हे इन्द्र, तुम निश्चय ही बहुत देना चाहते हो।
english: O giver of much, give us much; not little — bring much; O Indra, you indeed wish to give much.
notes: bhūridā is the vocative of bhūri-dāḥ.

hindi: क्योंकि तुम बहुत देने वाले के रूप में प्रसिद्ध हो, अनेक स्थानों पर, हे शूर, हे वृत्रहन्; हमें उदारता में भाग दो।
english: For you are famed as a giver of much, in many places, O hero, Vṛtra-slayer; give us a share in bounty.
notes: ā bhajasva is taken as 'give a share' (ā-√bhaj), with rādhasi 'in bounty'.

hindi: हे दूरदर्शी, मैं तुम्हारे दोनों भूरे को प्रकट करता हूँ, हे गोषण के वंशज; इन दोनों के पीछे गायों को ढीला न करो।
english: I proclaim your two brown ones, O far-seeing one, O descendant of the cow-winner; do not slacken the cows after these two.
notes: UNCLEAR throughout: babhrū (dual, 'two brown ones'), the referent of 'these two', and goṣaṇaḥ napāt (a name, 'Goṣan', or 'cow-winner'); the construction of mā ābhyām gāḥ anu śiśrathaḥ is not certain (the reading may be 'do not let go the cows after these two'). Rendered literally.

words.gram: m./n. loc. sg. form and sense uncertain

hindi: जैसे एक कन्या, चीरने वाले स्थान पर, नए छोटे काठ के खंभे पर, वैसे दोनों भूरे मार्गों पर शोभित होते हैं।
english: Like a young girl on a cleaving, on a new, small wooden post, the two brown ones shine on the courses.
notes: UNCLEAR: vidradhe (sense unknown, literally perhaps 'cleaving/splitting'); drupada 'wooden post' (literal). The whole simile cannot be resolved from the words; rendered literally. yāma = course/journey (could be 'watch').

words.gloss: for the one whose course is the bright
words.gram: m. dat. sg. bahuvrīhi form uncertain

words.gloss: for the one whose course follows the bright
words.gram: m. dat. sg. bahuvrīhi form uncertain

hindi: मेरे लिए पर्याप्त है, उसके लिए जिसका मार्ग प्रकाशमय है; पर्याप्त है, उसके लिए जिसका मार्ग उसके पीछे चलता है; दोनों भूरे मार्गों पर अचूक हैं।
english: Enough for me, for the one whose course is the bright; enough, for the one whose course follows the bright; the two brown ones are unfailing on the courses.
notes: UNCLEAR: usrayāmṇe and anusrayāmṇe may be names or epithets ('whose course is the rays/cows'); the decomposition is a guess. asridhā taken as nom. du. 'unfailing' (could be an adverb 'unfailingly'). The source ma is read as me by hiatus sandhi.
